drafted_from: tool:read-my-trading-account-board's own row (its words, input schema and sample run) and what its sample run answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Show my trading account board from my trading agent's last cycle", with {"cycle": {"attribute": "agent:trading-momentum.last-cycle", "value_json": "{\"cycle_id\": \"sample-cycle-1\", \"equity\": 100000, \"last_equity\": 99000, \"daily_pl_pct\": 1.01, \"target_pct\": 5, \"on_target\": false, \"buying_power\": 200000, \"positions\": [{\"symbol\": \"AAPL260116C00150000\", \"qty\": 2, \"market_value\": 1200}, {\"symbol\": \"BREAD\", \"qty\": 10, \"market_value\": 900}]}"}}. It runs tool:read-my-trading-account-board and answers the hero (value, today's change, goal), the account's own figures and the holdings, each option contract with its label. It reads only what you give it: nothing is sent to a broker.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes the trading agent's last cycle as input and answers the board; it keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Show my trading account board from my trading agent's last cycle", and give it the cycle fact the store holds for agent:trading-momentum.last-cycle (its value_json, or the cycle object itself).
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:read-my-trading-account-board and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: live (false means no readable cycle was given), headline (value, deltaValue, deltaPct, goalLabel), account (the cycle's own figures) and positions (one record per holding, with a label for each option contract).
4. Give a new cycle fact each time you want a fresh board: the answer is only as new as the cycle it was given.

worked_examples.title: Show the board from the last cycle on its own sample
worked_examples.ask: Show my trading account board from my trading agent's last cycle
worked_examples.given: The cycle fact with equity 100000, last equity 99000, daily P&L 1.01%, target 5% a day, buying power 200000, and two holdings: an AAPL call with strike 150 expiring Jan 16 2026, and 10 BREAD shares.
worked_examples.hands_back: It answered {"live": true, "headline": {"live": true, "value": "$100,000.00", "deltaValue": "+$1,000.00", "deltaPct": "+1.01%", "deltaTone": "up", "goalLabel": "20% of the 5% daily goal", "goalProgressPct": 20.200000000000003, "equitySeries": [99000, 100000]}, "account": {"id": "account", "cycle_id": "sample-cycle-1", "equity": 100000, "last_equity": 99000, "daily_pl_pct": 1.01, "target_pct": 5, "on_target": false, "buying_power": 200000}, "positions": [{"id": "AAPL260116C00150000", "payload": {"symbol": "AAPL260116C00150000", "qty": 2, "market_value": 1200, "id": "AAPL260116C00150000", "label": "AAPL $150 Call \u00b7 Jan 16 '26"}}, {"id": "BREAD", "payload": {"symbol": "BREAD", "qty": 10, "market_value": 900, "id": "BREAD"}}]}. The hero reads $100,000.00, +$1,000.00 (+1.01%), 20% of the 5% daily goal; the option holding reads "AAPL $150 Call · Jan 16 '26".
